title: The Replication Problem
text:
Replication studies have become a central concern in psychology. When researchers attempt to repeat published experiments, many find that the original effects are weaker than reported.

Some scientists argue that the problem lies in small sample sizes and selective publication. Others contend that replication failures are a normal part of the scientific process, because every experiment depends on specific conditions.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do many researchers find when they repeat published experiments?
options: The original effects are weaker than reported
Replication is too expensive to attempt
The results are identical each time

questions.text: What do some scientists identify as a cause of the problem, according to paragraph two?
options: Small sample sizes and selective publication

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of replication failures?
options: They are a predictable and normal part of research
They always prove that the original study was false
They should be avoided by all scientists

questions.text: Why might some scientists consider a failed replication unsurprising?
options: Experiments depend on specific conditions that may differ from one lab to another
Journals refuse to publish any results

vocabulary.definition: the act of repeating a study to check whether its results can be obtained again
choosing only some items from a larger group, often in a biased way
to state firmly that something is true, especially in an argument
a small group taken from a larger population for study

paragraph_translations: Дослідження відтворюваності стали центральною темою в психології. Коли дослідники намагаються повторити опубліковані експерименти, багато хто з них виявляє, що первинні ефекти слабші, ніж було заявлено.

Деякі вчені стверджують, що проблема полягає в малих вибірках і вибірковій публікації результатів. Інші заперечують, що невдачі відтворення є нормальною частиною наукового процесу, оскільки кожен експеримент залежить від конкретних умов.
